blocks.text: The piston in a compressor must be pushed back and forth by a connecting rod whose big end swings on a crank pin. To size the wrist-pin bearing and the inertia force on the piston you need the rod's angular acceleration at each crank angle, and that comes from relating the accelerations of its two ends.

blocks.markdown: Two points $A$ and $B$ on the same rigid body are a fixed distance apart, so $A$ can only move relative to $B$ by rotating about it. If $\mathbf r_{A/B}$ is the position of $A$ relative to $B$ (m), $\omega$ the body's angular velocity (rad/s) and $\alpha$ its angular acceleration (rad/s$^2$), the relative acceleration has two parts: a **tangential** part due to $\alpha$ and a **centripetal (normal)** part due to $\omega$.

blocks.caption: $(\mathbf a_{A/B})_t=\boldsymbol\alpha\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$ has magnitude $\alpha r$ perpendicular to $AB$; $(\mathbf a_{A/B})_n=-\omega^2\mathbf r_{A/B}$ has magnitude $\omega^2r$ along $AB$, directed from $A$ toward $B$.

blocks.title: Tangential and centripetal components
blocks.text: The **tangential component** $\alpha r$ is perpendicular to the line $AB$, in the sense of $\alpha$ (counterclockwise $\alpha$ pushes $A$ counterclockwise about $B$). The **centripetal component** $\omega^2r$ lies along $AB$ and always points from $A$ toward the reference point $B$. Their magnitudes combine as $a_{A/B}=r\sqrt{\alpha^2+\omega^4}$.

blocks.title: Acceleration of one end of a link
blocks.prompt: Point $B$ has acceleration 6 m/s$^2$ in the $+x$ direction. The link $BA$ is 0.8 m long, lies along $+x$ from $B$ to $A$, and has $\omega=2$ rad/s and $\alpha=5$ rad/s$^2$ counterclockwise. Find $\mathbf a_A$.

steps.text: Centripetal part: magnitude $\omega^2r$ directed from $A$ toward $B$, i.e. $-x$.
Tangential part: counterclockwise $\alpha$ moves $A$, which is on the $+x$ side of $B$, in $+y$.

blocks.markdown: **Connecting rod procedure.** For a slider-crank (crank $OA$, rod $AB$, slider $B$ on the $x$-axis): (1) find $\omega_3$ of the rod from the **velocity** equation $\mathbf v_B=\mathbf v_A+\boldsymbol\omega_3\times\mathbf r_{B/A}$ with $\mathbf v_B$ along $x$; (2) find $\mathbf a_A=-\omega_2^2\mathbf r_{A/O}+\boldsymbol\alpha_2\times\mathbf r_{A/O}$ for the crank; (3) write $\mathbf a_B=\mathbf a_A+\alpha_3\hat k\times\mathbf r_{B/A}-\omega_3^2\mathbf r_{B/A}$ and require $\mathbf a_B$ to be along $x$. The $y$-component gives $\alpha_3$, and the $x$-component gives $a_B$.

blocks.title: Rod at the crank vertical position
blocks.prompt: A slider-crank has crank $OA=0.10$ m turning at a constant $\omega_2=50$ rad/s counterclockwise, and rod $AB=0.40$ m. Find $\alpha_3$ and the slider acceleration when the crank is vertical ($A$ directly above $O$).

steps.text: Set up the geometry: with the crank vertical, A is at (0, 0.10) m and the slider B lies on the x-axis at x = sqrt(0.40^2 - 0.10^2) = 0.3873 m, so the vector from A to B is as shown. Also omega_3 = 0 at this instant, because v_A is purely horizontal and the slider can only move horizontally.
Acceleration of $A$ with constant crank speed.
With $\omega_3=0$, $\mathbf a_B=\mathbf a_A+\alpha_3(0.10,\,0.3873)$. The $y$-component must be zero.

blocks.caption: Components of relative acceleration of two points on a rigid body.

blocks.title: Order of work
blocks.text: Always do the velocity analysis first. The acceleration equation needs $\omega$ for the centripetal terms, and the unknowns ($\alpha$ and a slider's acceleration) come out of the two scalar components.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.text: Pointing the centripetal term away from the reference point, using $\omega$ of the crank for the rod's centripetal term, assigning the tangential direction with the wrong sign, and skipping the velocity analysis.

items: Use $\mathbf a_A=\mathbf a_B+\boldsymbol\alpha\times\mathbf r_{A/B}-\omega^2\mathbf r_{A/B}$ for any two points on the same rigid body.
Decide the line of action of every unknown before you solve.
At a dead-centre position the rod has $\omega_3=0$, and for constant crank speed $\alpha_3=0$ there.

points: Relative acceleration of two points on a rigid body is tangential $\alpha r$ plus centripetal $\omega^2r$ along the link toward the reference point.
Resolve vectors in two directions and solve; always find $\omega$ from velocities first.
For a connecting rod, the vertical component of the acceleration equation gives $\alpha_3$ because the slider moves along $x$ only.

questions.stem: Two points $A$ and $B$ lie on the same rigid body, which rotates with angular velocity $\omega$. In which direction does the centripetal component of $\mathbf a_{A/B}$ act?

options.text: Along the line $AB$, directed from $A$ toward $B$
Along the line $AB$, directed from $B$ toward $A$
Perpendicular to $AB$ in the sense of $\alpha$
In the direction of the velocity of $A$

questions.correctOptionText: Along the line $AB$, directed from $A$ toward $B$

distractorRationale.b: That would point away from the reference point, which is the wrong sign.
distractorRationale.d: Velocity direction is perpendicular to the line to the centre of rotation, not along it.

questions.explanation: The centripetal term is $-\omega^2\mathbf r_{A/B}$, which points opposite to $\mathbf r_{A/B}$ (from $B$ to $A$), i.e. from $A$ toward $B$. Its magnitude is $\omega^2r$.

questions.stem: A rigid link $AB$ of length 0.6 m turns with angular velocity 5 rad/s. Find the magnitude of the centripetal component of the acceleration of $A$ relative to $B$ in m/s$^2$.
questions.explanation: The centripetal component is $\omega^2r=5^2(0.6)=15$ m/s$^2$, directed from $A$ toward $B$.

questions.stem: A rigid link $AB$ of length 0.5 m has $\omega=3$ rad/s and $\alpha=8$ rad/s$^2$. Find the magnitude, in m/s$^2$, of the total acceleration of $A$ relative to $B$.
questions.explanation: The centripetal part is $\omega^2r=9(0.5)=4.5$ m/s$^2$ and the tangential part is $\alpha r=8(0.5)=4.0$ m/s$^2$. They are perpendicular, so $a=\sqrt{4.5^2+4.0^2}=6.02$ m/s$^2$.

questions.stem: Point $B$ of a link has acceleration 6 m/s$^2$ in the $+x$ direction. The link is 0.8 m long and lies along $+x$ from $B$ to $A$. Its angular velocity is 2 rad/s and its angular acceleration is 5 rad/s$^2$ counterclockwise. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $A$ in m/s$^2$.
questions.explanation: The centripetal part is $\omega^2r=3.2$ m/s$^2$ toward $B$ ($-x$), and the tangential part is $\alpha r=4.0$ m/s$^2$ in $+y$. So $\mathbf a_A=(6-3.2,\,4.0)=(2.8,\,4.0)$ m/s$^2$ with magnitude $4.88$ m/s$^2$.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly relates the accelerations of two points on the same rigid body in plane motion?

distractorRationale.a: The sign of the centripetal term is wrong; it points toward the reference point.
distractorRationale.b: This is the velocity relation, with $\omega$ in place of $\alpha$ and missing the $\omega^2$ term.
distractorRationale.d: The terms have wrong dimensions; $\omega^2$ and a cross product are needed.

questions.explanation: The tangential term is $\boldsymbol\alpha\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$ and the normal term is $-\omega^2\mathbf r_{A/B}$. Both are required because points on a rigid body move in circles about each other.

questions.stem: A slider-crank has crank $r=0.12$ m, connecting rod $l=0.45$ m and a crank speed of 40 rad/s (constant, counterclockwise). The crank angle is $60^\circ$ above the line of stroke. Find the magnitude of the connecting rod's angular acceleration in rad/s$^2$.
questions.explanation: Positions: $A=(0.06,\,0.1039)$ m and $B=(0.4978,\,0)$ m, so $B-A$ has $x$-component 0.4378 m. The velocity equation gives $\omega_3=-5.48$ rad/s (clockwise). The $y$-component of the acceleration equation gives $\alpha_3=(\omega_2^2-\omega_3^2)y_A/0.4378=(1600-30.0)(0.1039)/0.4378=372.6$ rad/s$^2$ (counterclockwise).

questions.stem: A slider-crank turns at constant crank speed and the crank is at the dead-centre position (crank and connecting rod collinear along the line of stroke). What is the angular acceleration of the connecting rod?

options.text: Maximum, because the rod is aligned with the line of stroke
Zero, because the vertical acceleration of the crank pin is zero and the rod is aligned with the stroke
Equal to the crank angular acceleration

questions.correctOptionText: Zero, because the vertical acceleration of the crank pin is zero and the rod is aligned with the stroke

distractorRationale.a: The vertical component of $\mathbf a_A$ is zero, so there is nothing to produce $\alpha_3$.
distractorRationale.c: The crank has constant speed so its $\alpha_2=0$, and the rod is a different body.
distractorRationale.d: This has the wrong dimensions for an angular acceleration.

questions.explanation: At dead centre $A$ lies on the line of stroke, so $\mathbf a_A=-\omega_2^2\mathbf r_{A/O}$ is along the stroke, and $\omega_3=0$. The $y$-component of $\mathbf a_B=\mathbf a_A+\alpha_3\hat k\times\mathbf r_{B/A}$ then requires $\alpha_3\,l=0$, so $\alpha_3=0$.

questions.stem: At a certain instant a link has zero angular velocity but a non-zero angular acceleration $\alpha$. How does point $A$ accelerate relative to point $B$ on the link, separated by distance $r$?

options.text: Not at all, because the velocities are equal
Purely tangentially, with magnitude $\alpha r$ perpendicular to $AB$

questions.correctOptionText: Purely tangentially, with magnitude $\alpha r$ perpendicular to $AB$

distractorRationale.a: The along-link component is $\omega^2r$, which vanishes when $\omega=0$.
distractorRationale.b: Equal (zero relative) velocity does not imply zero relative acceleration.
distractorRationale.c: With $\omega=0$ the centripetal component is zero.

questions.explanation: With $\omega=0$ the term $-\omega^2\mathbf r_{A/B}$ vanishes, leaving only $\boldsymbol\alpha\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$, whose magnitude is $\alpha r$ and whose direction is perpendicular to $AB$.

questions.stem: A student writes the relative acceleration of two points on a link as $\alpha r$ only. Explain why this is incomplete, define the tangential and centripetal components with their magnitudes and directions, and say when each is zero.
markingGuide: Relative acceleration has two components for a rotating link
Tangential component $\alpha r$, perpendicular to $AB$, in the sense of $\alpha$
Centripetal component $\omega^2r$, along $AB$ directed toward the reference point
Tangential is zero when $\alpha=0$ (constant angular velocity)
Centripetal is zero when $\omega=0$ (instantaneously at rest or translating)
questions.explanation: Even at constant angular velocity a point moving in a circle accelerates toward the centre. The centripetal term is therefore always present when the link turns.

questions.stem: Outline the procedure for finding the angular acceleration of the connecting rod of a slider-crank at a given crank angle, stating the equations used and explaining why the velocity analysis must come first.
markingGuide: Find positions and the slider location from geometry
Velocity equation $\mathbf v_B=\mathbf v_A+\boldsymbol\omega_3\times\mathbf r_{B/A}$ with $\mathbf v_B$ along the stroke gives $\omega_3$
Crank pin acceleration $\mathbf a_A=-\omega_2^2\mathbf r_{A/O}+\boldsymbol\alpha_2\times\mathbf r_{A/O}$
Writes $\mathbf a_B=\mathbf a_A+\boldsymbol\alpha_3\times\mathbf r_{B/A}-\omega_3^2\mathbf r_{B/A}$ with $\mathbf a_B$ along the stroke
Takes the component perpendicular to the stroke to get $\alpha_3$, then the stroke component for $a_B$; explains $\omega_3$ is needed for the centripetal term
questions.explanation: Only two unknowns remain ($\alpha_3$ and $a_B$) once the line of action of $\mathbf a_B$ is known, so the two scalar components solve the problem. The velocity step is needed because $\omega_3^2$ appears in the acceleration equation.
